description: We are Lazy MeowMeow, a passionate team of problem-solvers, space enthusiasts, and developers. Humanity left behind footprints, scientific instruments, and spacecraft on the Moon—monuments to our first steps into the cosmos. Team Lazy MeowMeow is dedicated to bringing these forgotten lunar relics back into focus.
summary:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive educational simulation that targets young teens and transforms NASA's abandoned space equipment into an exciting space archaeology experience. Players take on the role of a NASA Space Archaeologist, discovering historic artifacts left behind on the Moon, Mars, and other celestial bodies. They can explore each artifact in 3D, rotate it, separate it into individual components, and investigate how each piece works and contributed to its original mission.

It also addresses this challenge by making space exploration history engaging and hands-on, rather than relying on traditional quizzes or reading materials. Through interactive disassembly, animations, and detailed explanations, players learn about the science, engineering, and history behind real NASA technology.

This project matters because abandoned spacecraft and scientific instruments are more than forgotten equipment; they are evidence of humanity's achievements in space. Exploring them can help develop critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and an interest in technology, engineering, and space exploration.
details:
OrbitDrop is an educational adventure game inspired by NASA's space missions. Players explore the Moon, Mars, and other locations to discover historic spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific equipment. They complete missions, collect evidence, answer science questions, earn XP and credits, and unlock rewards. A mentor character also guides players and explains scientific concepts.

Three unique crew members join players. Cyborg, the tech-savvy systems guide from Teen Titans, explains space technology and NASA telemetry with humour and energy. Kairo, a lively, adventurous cosmic scavenger, spots forgotten spacecraft and adds excitement to exploration. Cmdr. Mochi, a deadpan tuxedo cat and signal analyst, monitors deep-space signals and keeps players on their toes with witty reactions to incorrect answers.

One of the game's key features is its 3D Disassembly Lab, where players can examine historical NASA artifacts up close. By selecting individual parts of an artifact, they learn its purpose during the mission, how it functioned, and what eventually happened to it. Turning complex engineering information into an interactive learning experience that seems more enjoyable.

The project encourages curiosity, problem-solving, and an interest in STEM subjects while helping players understand the history and achievements of space exploration. It also highlights how equipment can continue to have scientific and historical value even after a mission has ended.

The game was developed with the assistance of Google AI Studio and Gemini AI, using web development technologies such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Its creative features include 3D artifact exploration. It is designed to run in a web browser on a computer or laptop.

Its creativity comes from combining real NASA mission information with fictional storytelling, animated environments, sound effects, quizzes, and rewards. During development, we considered scientific accuracy, teenage interests, increasing difficulty, ease of use, and the balance between education and entertainment.

Overall, the project uses gaming to bring space exploration history to life and inspire the youth to take an interest in science and technology.
